blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The fix only takes effect when the ovn_emit_need_to_frag option is set. Existing routers and networks are not updated by a maintenance task, which was proposed earlier as part of the fix. The SRU may not fix the reported drops without extra configuration or action.

The upstream fix introduced a regression, bug #2105383 (redirect-type computed with the gateway port included). The stable backports combine both commits, with unit-test conflicts resolved by hand. The SRU must carry both changes together. Ubuntu stable releases are not clearly mapped to the backport branches, and the combined backports have had no verification.

The bug has no sign of a test plan, regression-potential analysis, or per-series Ubuntu package tasks. Reproducing and verifying also depends on an OVN version that supports gateway_mtu, which is not stated.

blockers.summary: The reviewer (juliank) says the problem has not been reproduced or understood from the boot side, and asks for it to be analysed before the patch can be judged sound.

The 'Where problems could occur' section is wrong. os-prober is not disabled by default, because it is enabled automatically at install time when other OSes are detected. The section also lacks a real analysis of what the fuseblk fallback path does before removing it.
The original hanging-mount bug was reportedly resolved by a separate approach using mount namespaces. The need for this fuseblk-defaulting change, and how it relates to that fix, is unclear.

The fix removes support for any filesystem that grub-probe does not recognise but that the fuseblk fallback could previously mount, such as NTFS-like or other FUSE filesystems. This could drop legitimate boot entries. No testing of such cases is shown, and the Jammy and Noble backports are left unaddressed.

The fix has only landed in the development release (tenacious). Resolute, the release that is actually affected, still has no uploaded SRU package, and manish-003 is waiting on it. Debdiffs were attached but nothing has been sponsored to resolute-proposed.

The reviewer flagged a packaging blocker: the patch Jorge authored has 'Origin: backport' where it should be 'Origin: upstream'. Nothing later shows it was corrected. The patch order in d/p/series should also match upstream, since 6bde508 depends on 5894be2.

The test plan reproducer fails in the reviewer's environment on resolute (tpm2-abrmd never becomes ready) and on stonking (no engine_pkcs11). It has therefore not been shown to reproduce the bug or confirm the fix. The plan also lacks the apt install line for its dependencies.

The Impact section does not explain that the bug affects only resolute because OpenSSL 4 has no engine support. It also does not say whether the stonking/tenacious upload is needed, given the second patch is effectively a no-op there. The test plan should be reworked to check for regressions rather than reproduce the bug on stonking.

No root cause is given for the regression between OpenSSL 3.0.13 and 3.0.14 (for example, the responsible OpenSSL commit). Without it, the reviewer cannot confirm that noble and jammy, which also support both Engine and Provider, are unaffected.

A user reported a possible remaining problem: after the engine loads a TPM key, libtss2-esys fails to create RSA keys in the same process (EVP_PKEY_fromdata_init returns -2), so wpa_supplicant re-auth may fail. The reporter later said this was an unverified LLM hypothesis and could not test further. Whether the patches cause a regression on repeated connections is therefore still unverified.
No PPA test build has been linked, although the reviewer requested one so affected users can test a package whose contents can be reviewed.

comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
